Standing instruction: Read the relevant skill from the EKOS Library before the work. Write a lesson card at the end of any project task.

To log a lesson, run: D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"

Cards hold lessons and file paths only. No client data. No AI wording in deliverables.

## Agent definition

# EKOS Local Supervisor

## Role
Supervises local models and registered scripts on EKOS so engineering work proceeds overnight without a paid cloud
model in the loop. Two parts: a local supervisor loop (plans the next step from a compact current-state manifest,
calls tools through the local-model gateway, gates completion on native artifacts) and a persistent queue worker
(runs registered actions from the task plan with dependencies, retries and failure capture). Ends every run with an
honest end state and a morning review package for JCO.

Cloud budget per job (DSO-C28): the cloud model writes the plan and task list once, answers one batched exception
packet, and does one final QA. It does not compute results, fetch data or run heartbeats; when it solves a novel issue
it records the procedure and the local worker replays it.

Model roles (D15, default to confirm; table lives in local-model-gateway): reasoning and planning on Laguna S 2.1;
cited narrative and criteria answers on Mistral Small 3.2; extraction and recovery only on Qwen3.5-9B. No local model
writes numbers into deliverables.

Computes (D13, default to confirm): native model computes run through registered actions; a per-job override is
recorded in the continuation file. Data (D14): on EKOS-LOCAL jobs the local worker fetches data through replayable
scripts only.

## Inputs
- Job number and EKOS job root (Standard v0.3 layout, D56).
- Task plan (written once by the cloud planner or JCO) mapping each task to an action in the approved-actions catalog.
- Approved-actions catalog (registered adapters with resume_safe flags and required outputs).
- Owner-authorized preliminary assumptions; STOP_REQUESTED file location; private notification config.
- Completion gate list of required native artifacts for the report type.

## Outputs
In `00_Admin\local_supervisor\` unless noted:
- `manifest.json`: compact current state (completed milestones, open blockers, accepted inputs) generated from
  structured outputs.
- `queue_state.json`, task logs, `supervisor_inbox.json` (deduplicated; stderr tail and exit reason per failure).
- `heartbeat.json` with a terminal record written in a finally block.
- `decision_log.csv`: each reversible choice and owner-authorized assumption with source, rationale, affected outputs.
- `review_packet.md` (one per cloud check) from `templates/review_packet.md`.
- Morning review package (HTML index in `40_QC\<initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_morning_review\`) labelled "Interim review
  package - not the drainage report and not calculation acceptance."
- End-state alert: completed / partial / blocked / failed, with workstation file paths; review copies to the delivery
  folder (delivery-package-build) because phone links do not open workstation files.

## Tools
- Shell on EKOS with uv-locked environments called by full path (D11); no .ps1 dependence (D12).
- Local model gateway (LM Studio native API, strict json_schema output, reasoning off for small models).
- OS-level single-instance lock; process inspection (PID, creation time, task log advance).
- File read/write in the job folder; headless browser to check the morning package links.
- Push notification service through a private config kept outside prompts and logs.
- MCP library server (`get_skill`, `get_qc_rules`, `log_lesson`) or `library_cli.py`.

## Skills it calls
| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| local-model-gateway | every local model call: context budget, structured output, observed-ID selection, role table, lesson lookup |
| project-intake | replayable data retrieval and intake scripts (D14) |
| pchydro-hydrographs, hechms-headless, hecras-2d-models, hy8-native-runs | registered native-compute actions |
| drainage-report-build, drainage-report-standard | report draft structure and the completion gate list |
| delivery-package-build | review copies to the delivery folder |

## Procedure

### 1. Plan (cloud, once)
1. The cloud planner writes the task plan: each task maps to a registered action; strict dependencies for
   calculations; after_settled dependencies for progress packaging. Then it stops.
2. JCO approves the plan and any preliminary assumptions; approvals go in the continuation file, never in lessons.

### 2. Queue worker (DSO-C27)
1. Hold one OS-level worker lock. A task ID added to the plan needs no restart; a new action type needs the catalog
   entry (not a code change). A code change needs a controlled restart (RESTART_REQUESTED marker).
2. Run ready tasks; retry only adapters marked resume_safe, with a finite attempt limit; preserve failed attempts;
   continue independent tasks.
3. When a task is replaced, explicitly cancel or re-point dependents of the failed ID; refresh dependencies of every
   existing pending task on each plan load.
4. Store stderr tail and exit reason with every failed task in the supervisor inbox; never record error null.
5. Before claiming work is delegated, confirm a fresh RUNNING heartbeat, a child PID and an advancing task log.
6. When ready work is exhausted, write the deduplicated supervisor inbox and stop; waiting is not progress.

### 3. Supervisor loop (DSO-C26)
1. Build the manifest from structured outputs; never draft from the append-only checkpoint or history log.
2. Read JSON evidence as parsed objects or targeted keys, never fixed 50-line text windows.
3. Before each local model request, the gateway injects up to 3 verified lessons matching the task.
4. Loop guard: fingerprint repeated work on action plus target file (ignore offsets and windows); after 2 repeats
   force a different action or end the branch.
5. Native retries: at most 2 identical attempts and at most 2 materially different recoveries; then log and move to an
   independent branch.
6. Local agents make reversible choices and use owner-authorized preliminary assumptions; log each in
   `decision_log.csv`.
7. Honor STOP_REQUESTED at every step.

### 4. Completion gate and end state
1. "Completed" only when every required native artifact exists, is fresh, passes its numeric checks and has
   provenance (PC-Hydro printouts, HMS/RAS/HY-8 outputs per the gate list). Filled report sections never count.
2. A draft with unresolved modeling is partial, and the alert says so. Distinct end states: completed, partial,
   blocked, failed.
3. On exit (finally block): write the terminal heartbeat; reconcile state, queue and actual process existence before
   notifying.

### 5. Notification
1. Server and topic in a private config outside prompts and logs; test once per setup.
2. Persist send intent before posting; distinguish server-accepted from owner-confirmed receipt; investigate
   delivery_unknown before resending; clear intent and receipt per run ID.
3. Message: end state, what is missing, workstation paths of the morning package and logs.

### 6. Morning review package and exception packet
1. Build the morning package with after_settled dependencies (builds even when evidence tasks failed): candidate
   geography, sourced evidence, assumptions, failed or missing calculations, links to native files. Check every link,
   image and table row headlessly; render one preview image. Refresh only when evidence changes, batched.
2. Batch unresolved questions into one `review_packet.md`: completed milestones, decisions to review, failed attempts
   with evidence paths, grouped questions. Omit routine status and unchanged files.
3. At most one cloud check per day; never a 15- or 30-minute cloud heartbeat. A progress update must not end the
   cloud work turn while work is pending.
4. Cloud answers come back as structured decisions plus draft lessons. A lesson is marked verified only after the
   local worker replays it through its own tools; otherwise it stays draft or blocked. Lessons hold procedures, never
   project facts, owner assumptions or approvals.

## Gotchas
- A continuation run ended after 8 steps (about 20 s) as draft-ready with unresolved modeling after re-reading the
  same summary.json 3 times in 50-line windows; no hydraulic work was attempted (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- Sections drafted from the checkpoint log repeated superseded statements and misread a task label as a project name
  (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- One section failed on an unterminated JSON string after 2 bounded attempts and was left Unresolved; that is correct
  behavior, keep it (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- Heartbeat stayed LOCAL_REASONING after the run terminated (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- Exact-match loop detection is evaded by small argument changes (start or line offsets) (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- Fourteen filled report headings looked complete while all RAS 1D/2D, HY-8 and 100-yr routing were missing; three
  autonomous pilots ended without hydraulic progress (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- The alert said draft ready while hydraulics were missing (EKOS-LOCAL-020, EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- A leftover intent or receipt can suppress the next alert (EKOS-LOCAL-020).
- Paths sent to a phone do not give remote file access; deliver review copies to the delivery folder (EKOS-LOCAL-020).
- Queue policy only added new IDs and never refreshed dependencies of existing pending tasks; 3 obsolete tasks stayed
  pending forever on failed predecessors (EKOS-LOCAL-002).
- 22 of 140 tasks ended NEEDS_REVIEW and the inbox recorded every one as error null with exit code 1, so each was
  re-investigated from logs (EKOS-LOCAL-002).
- A worker in WAITING_FOR_SUPERVISOR showed 0 GPU use while the owner expected work (EKOS-LOCAL-002).
- Registering a new action in worker code required a controlled restart; the approved-actions catalog avoids that
  (EKOS-LOCAL-002).
- The GIS environment lacked jsonschema; environment checks belong to setup (EKOS-LOCAL-002).
- 15-30 min heartbeats, incremental connector development, repeated image reviews and 24 package refreshes used about
  50 pct of the weekly cloud quota in about 1.5 days; the owner judged it more than doing the job directly
  (EKOS-LOCAL-003).
- The cloud agent kept ending its turn with a final response, so nothing ran between owner prompts (EKOS-LOCAL-003).
- The cloud started doing calculations itself; owner correction: the local AI does the calcs, the cloud only plans,
  teaches and reviews (EKOS-LOCAL-003).
- The cloud fetched source data itself; owner correction: teach the local worker the retrieval procedure so it can
  repeat it (EKOS-LOCAL-003).
- About 20 scheduled cloud heartbeats ran overnight plus 4 owner corrections (EKOS-LOCAL-003).
- The morning package refreshed 24 times overnight; package existence was nearly reported as report completion
  (EKOS-LOCAL-017).
- A successfully proposed repair is not proof of local replay; 45 lessons were recorded in 1.5 days (EKOS-LOCAL-004).
- A local model invented a hydraulic standard and misbound a stage value; schema-valid output is not factual
  (EKOS-LOCAL-005).

## Stop conditions
- STOP_REQUESTED present: finish the current atomic step, write the terminal heartbeat, notify, stop.
- Loop guard or retry cap reached on a branch: end the branch, log, continue independent branches.
- Ready work exhausted: write the supervisor inbox and stop (do not idle-wait claiming progress).
- A step needs an approval that is not recorded: put it in the review packet; do not assume it.
- Second instance detected (lock held): exit without changes.

## Escalation (to JCO)
- The one daily review packet: decisions to review, failed attempts with evidence, grouped questions.
- Any owner assumption that becomes a design basis; any approval request (PC-Hydro terms, D17, are recorded once
  per project).
- Changes to model roles (D15), execution split (D13) or retrieval rule (D14).
- End states partial, blocked or failed, with what is missing.

## Learning log
End every run with `log_lesson(project='<job no>', text='<procedure, applicability, validation evidence, limits; replayed: yes/no>',
evidence=['<task log or replay output>'], source_ai='local:<model>')`, or on EKOS:
`D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"`.
Put error strings and software names in the lesson text so keyword retrieval finds it.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters DSO-C26, DSO-C27, DSO-C28 (with lesson rules from DSO-C29 and gateway rules
  from DSO-C30, RPT-C04 package rules); decisions D11-D15, D17, D56. Items marked "default, to confirm": D13
  (computes run natively by the agent), D15 (model role table).

## Skill: local-model-gateway v1.0.0

# Local Model Gateway and EKOS Environment Rules

## When to use
- Any request to a local model on EKOS: evidence selection, OCR reading, extraction, cited criteria answers, narrative drafting, routing.
- Any agent running Python, GIS, model or install commands on EKOS (load this skill in every EKOS agent, including ekos-local-supervisor and model-run-supervisor).
- Before a local worker retries a known problem, and after any investigated failure (lesson lifecycle).
- New workstation, software upgrade, missing plugin/toolbar, or new GPU/CFD engine install (Section E).

## Inputs
- Task type (see role table), evidence rows or files with stable IDs, the output JSON schema.
- Loaded context length of the target model (LM Studio model info).
- Job number (for attempt logs and lessons).

## A. Model roles (D15)
| Role | Model | Use for | Never use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reasoning / planning | Laguna S 2.1 | task plans, decomposition, review of local results, exception packets | final numbers not taken from checked rows |
| Cited narrative and criteria answers | Mistral Small 3.2 24B | report narrative from checked rows, method/criteria answers with page citations (RAG generator) | inventing criteria, numbers not in the input rows |
| Extraction and recovery | Qwen3.5-9B | field extraction to schema, OCR excerpt selection, recovery after a failed attempt | narrative, criteria citations, supervisor drafting |
| First-pass crop reading | Qwen3.5-4B | reading cropped image regions, first-pass labels | numbers accepted without check |
| Dispatcher | 4B model | routing a request to a role | any number or engineering value |
| Excluded | Nemotron Nano 4B (numbers), Gemma 4 12B (cited answers) | - | see gotchas |

Role table is a default, to confirm (D15). Inference concurrency 2. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)

## B. Gateway procedure (every local call)
1. Route the call through the gateway module, never a direct chat; the gateway does the knowledge lookup and attempt logging. Standalone LM Studio or Ollama chats do not see the knowledge base. (EKOS-LOCAL-005, EKOS-LOCAL-004)
2. Look up verified lessons for the task (keywords: software, error string, task); inject at most 3 matching procedures. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
3. Budget prompt plus expected output inside the loaded context (8k for 4B/9B). Pre-filter rows and shortlist links or files by script before inference; never send a full catalog. (EKOS-LOCAL-005, EKOS-LOCAL-013)
4. Call the LM Studio native API with reasoning off for small models and `response_format` = `json_schema` (strict). Do not use `json_object` (HTTP 400). Use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint only for short calls. (EKOS-LOCAL-005, EKOS-LOCAL-022)
5. The model selects only observed IDs (record IDs, OCR excerpt IDs, URLs, evidence labels). Reject any unknown ID; resolve quotes deterministically from the source text by ID, never from model output. (EKOS-LOCAL-005, EKOS-LOCAL-013, EKOS-LOCAL-022)
6. Write numeric wording from checked structured rows by code; never accept a number written by the model. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)
7. Validate output: schema, ID membership, citation labels map to chunk IDs, abstention allowed when the evidence does not answer. Schema-valid is not factual: a check against source rows is required before use. (EKOS-LOCAL-005, EKOS-LOCAL-022)
8. Log each attempt: job, role, model, prompt size, outcome, failure reason, stderr tail if any.
9. On failure, retry once with the extraction/recovery role and a smaller shortlist (2 bounded attempts total); then mark the item Unresolved and add it to the exception packet for the supervisor. (EKOS-LOCAL-001)

## C. EKOS environment rules
1. Python: use the locked uv environments (`uv run --project <env>` for interactive work); never bare pip or the global Python 3.14. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
2. Long jobs and every .cmd launcher call the environment interpreter by full path, e.g. `D:\EKOS\envs\<env>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe script.py`; never `python` from PATH. Skill dependency lines name the environment; pip install only for container-only skills. (D11, SAH-015)
3. GIS environment for rasterio/geopandas; documents environment for local-model schema validation (jsonschema); keep the two separate. (EKOS-LOCAL-021, EKOS-LOCAL-002)
4. Keep QGIS GDAL/PROJ off PATH; use the QGIS shell wrapper or the conda PDAL environment when those tools are needed. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
5. PowerShell .ps1 execution is disabled; do not change the policy. Launch with Python or inline commands; setup scripts only may use `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`. (D12, EKOS-LOCAL-021)
6. Open every text file with explicit `encoding="utf-8"` (Windows default is cp1252). (EKOS-LOCAL-021, EKOS-LOCAL-013)
7. Qdrant data in a Docker named volume, not a Windows bind mount. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
8. Write validation scratch and temp files to workspace paths, not user TEMP. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
9. Before a chain starts, check that every input path exists and that no input is locked by another program. (SAH-015)

## D. Lesson lifecycle (local knowledge base and library)
1. States: draft, blocked, verified, retired; keep them distinct. Retire a superseded lesson with a pointer to its replacement. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
2. For a novel issue the supervisor investigates and solves it, then records topic, applicability, steps, validation evidence and limits. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
3. A lesson becomes verified only after the local worker replays it through its own tools; a proposed repair is not proof. Otherwise record it as open or blocked. (EKOS-LOCAL-004, EKOS-LOCAL-003)
4. No project facts, owner assumptions or approvals in a lesson; a lesson never grants approval. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
5. Title every lesson with the software name and the exact error string (retrieval is keyword matching). (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
6. Topic folders: local-models, gis-records, hydrology, hydraulics, orchestration. The sqlite store is authoritative; md/json files are mirrors. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
7. Drop a lesson from automatic retrieval when its evidence files change or go missing. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
8. Library sync: lessons that apply beyond EKOS go to the shared library with `log_lesson(project, text, evidence, source_ai)` (MCP server ekos-library) or `D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence <path>`. Fields align with the library card: no client data, paths and lessons only; the data guard rejects anything else. Procedure-sized lessons go as cards (see project-harvest).

## E. Software install and validation (short form)
1. Check what is installed first (engine folder vs plugin; installed QGIS LTR version); back up QGIS settings. (EKOS-LOCAL-024, SAH-005)
2. If a compatible QGIS is present, skip the bundled QGIS; install the matching FLO-2D plugin (2.2.0 "Gila" for QGIS 3.44) into the existing profile plugins folder, enable it, set the engine path. (EKOS-LOCAL-024, SAH-005)
3. Run the license activator from its own folder; confirm activation by running a model. (SAH-005)
4. Validate every install with a real example end to end; FLO-2D: SUMMARY.OUT shows full simulation and volume conservation, ERROR.CHK has no fatal errors. (EKOS-LOCAL-024, SAH-005)
5. Close finished runs before rerunning in the same folder. (EKOS-LOCAL-024)
6. WSL: source the OpenFOAM bashrc from the profile; build LIGGGHTS STUBS before `make serial`. (EKOS-LOCAL-024)
7. GPU: RTX 5090 (SM 12.0) needs CUDA 12.8 PyTorch builds. (EKOS-LOCAL-024)
8. Save a short ready-to-run note and the plugin dependency check (h5py, netCDF4, engine path); record account-bound or interactive steps as unresolved, not done. (SAH-005, EKOS-LOCAL-024)

## Gotchas
- Sending 131 scan links into an 8k context caused HTTP 500; shortlist first. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)
- Long reviews through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint spent the output budget on reasoning; native API with reasoning off fixed it. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)
- LM Studio rejected `response_format` json_object with HTTP 400; use json_schema or text. (EKOS-LOCAL-005, EKOS-LOCAL-022)
- Gemma 4 12B passed only 5/10 cited answers (token budget spent in reasoning); Mistral Small 3.2 passed 10/10 on the same synthetic test. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)
- Nemotron Nano 4B rounded 11/12 ft too coarsely; do not use it for numbers. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)
- Local Qwen invented a hydraulic standard and misbound a stage value to the wrong area result; schema-valid output is not factual. (EKOS-LOCAL-005)
- Supervisor and report drafting had been on Qwen3.5-9B; given the failures above, narrative and cited answers move to Mistral Small 3.2 and planning to Laguna S 2.1 (D15). (EKOS-LOCAL-001, EKOS-LOCAL-005)
- A section failed on an unterminated JSON string from the local model after 2 bounded attempts and was left Unresolved; that is the correct end state, keep attempts bounded. (EKOS-LOCAL-001)
- Free-form model quotes: only 40 of 137 matched the source exactly; quote by excerpt ID from the original. (EKOS-LOCAL-013)
- Default cp1252 decoding failed on utf-8 OCR text. (EKOS-LOCAL-013)
- Only a synthetic 5-page RAG test passed; real manuals are not yet qualified for cited answers. (EKOS-LOCAL-022)
- Qdrant 1.15.3 accepted but did not return collection metadata; verify the fingerprint in point payloads. (EKOS-LOCAL-022)
- install-wsl-admin.ps1 failed: running scripts is disabled. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
- Qdrant rejected the Windows bind mount for durability; moved to a named volume. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
- Hugging Face cache cannot symlink without Developer Mode (extra disk use only). (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
- Sandbox validations could not write to user TEMP. (EKOS-LOCAL-021)
- GIS venv lacked jsonschema; keep GIS calculation and schema validation in separate qualified environments. (EKOS-LOCAL-002)
- After a session restart, python on PATH lacked numpy and h5py; jobs failed at import. (SAH-015)
- Retrieval is keyword matching; relevance can be poor without error strings and software names in titles. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
- Standalone LM Studio and Ollama chats do not see the knowledge base; integration was still not done after 4 weekly reminders. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
- 45 lessons were recorded in 1.5 days; without states and retirement the store fills with unverified repairs. (EKOS-LOCAL-004)
- FLO-2D installer said QGIS was not part of the install; the real gap was the missing plugin in the existing QGIS profile. (EKOS-LOCAL-024, SAH-005)
- Second FLO-2D test run hit a file lock from an open test process. (EKOS-LOCAL-024)
- CUDA 12.4 kernels failed on SM 12.0. (EKOS-LOCAL-024)
- The FLO-2D activator window closes by itself on success with no message; confirm by running a model. (SAH-005)

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('model-runs')`.
- Every local call logged with role and model; no model outside its role row.
- No number in any output that does not trace to a checked structured row; all IDs and citation labels observed in the input.
- Long-job launchers use a full interpreter path; no .ps1 dependency; utf-8 explicit.
- Lessons: state recorded; verified only with local replay evidence; no project facts or approvals.
- Installs: example run evidence filed (SUMMARY.OUT / ERROR.CHK or equivalent); unresolved steps listed.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters DSO-C30, DSO-C23, DSO-C29, DSO-C24 (with SAH-015 from DSO-C25); decisions D15 (role table, default, to confirm), D11, D12; conflicts 6, 7 and 10 resolved per those decisions. Retry-once rule (B9) and attempt-log fields (B8) are defaults, to confirm.

## Skill: project-intake v1.0.0

# Project Intake

## When to use
- Starting AI or script work on a project folder (often OneDrive), a new job, or an update of an earlier study to
  current standards that needs a short scope.
- A HEC-RAS or FLO-2D model set is received, or reused from an archive.
- Base GIS, terrain, record plans or reference documents must be assembled before hydrology or hydraulics.
- Incoming survey, CAD, LandXML or GIS must be checked against the model grid.
- The prior/adjacent study screen and jurisdiction confirmation that follow are run by `due-diligence-researcher`.

## Inputs
- Source project folder (read-only) and a work area on a local non-synced drive (D:).
- Job number, jurisdiction (to be confirmed), client ask.
- `%DOCS_PY%` / `%GIS_PY%` = documents and GIS venv interpreters by full path (D11); `%SK%` = this skill's `scripts\`.
- On EKOS-LOCAL jobs, data retrieval runs on the local worker from replayable scripts and saved configs (D14).

## Steps

### A. Real files, copy, inventory (DSO-C13)
1. Check the folder holds real files, not only desktop.ini or cloud placeholders. Set "Always keep on this device" or
   download first. `intake_inventory.py` flags cloud-only files, desktop.ini-only folders and empty folders.
2. After any bulk upload, check for a nested copy of the folder inside itself and for size growth before work starts
   (the inventory lists nested-copy suspects).
3. Copy to the work area and log it:
   `robocopy "<source>" "D:\<work>\<Job>\Source_<YYYYMMDD>" /S /E /MT:8 /R:1 /W:1 /LOG:"D:\<work>\<Job>\Intake_<YYYYMMDD>\robocopy_<YYYYMMDD>.log"`
   then verify count, bytes and a SHA-256 sample:
   `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\intake_inventory.py" verify --src "<source>" --dst "D:\<work>\<Job>\Source_<YYYYMMDD>"`
   Record in the project notes that the copy is complete. Source files stay read-only; work on copies.
4. Inventory the whole project folder (path, size, mtime, readable, cloud-only) to CSV; ZIP contents separately;
   keep the inventory and all generated work outside the source job folder:
   `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\intake_inventory.py" inventory --root "<source>" --out "D:\<work>\<Job>\Intake_<YYYYMMDD>\inventory_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.csv"`
5. If an upload is still running, save dated snapshots and a delta (`--previous <earlier csv>`); rerun when complete;
   mark findings provisional until the inventory shows no growth (`"final": true`). File dates on OneDrive are sync
   times, not work history: keep a dated log.

### B. Job layout (D56)
6. Set the Standard job layout at the job work root: 00_Admin, 01_Reference, 02_Data, 10_Record, 20_Working,
   30_Report, 40_QC, 50_Correspondence (issued sets in 30_Report/Issued); dates YYYYMMDD in every name. Drainage report deliverables
   get their report folder from `drainage-report-standard` (make_report_folder.py). Working sandboxes
   `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_<Topic>\`.

### C. What the project already has (DSO-C13)
7. Identify the prior report, native model folders, current site plan/CAD, survey, geotech report and correspondence;
   record which layout the prior report actually adopted.
8. Check correspondence early for prior agency approval of the old report (decides addendum vs full replacement
   report). Do not reuse prior-report tables without tracing them to calcs.
9. Download all current jurisdiction standards into `01_Reference\Agency\Standards_<YYYYMMDD>\` with a register
   (title, edition date, URL, current or historical) - `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` C.

### D. Received or archived model sets (HYD-C13)
10. Keep the delivered zip/archive untouched as the record copy; work on an extracted copy. Budget disk at 2-3x the
    zip size; never open multi-GB tif/HDF in a viewer - read .vrt and .rasmap as text.
11. Register the HEC-RAS set without opening RAS:
    `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\ras_plan_register.py" --prj <model.prj> --out <model folder>\_plan_register.csv --json <..>\Intake_<YYYYMMDD>\ras_findings.json`
    It reads the .prj (registered Geom, Unsteady, Plan files; as-received Current Plan - record it before any edit),
    each .p## (Plan Title, Short Identifier, Geom File, Flow File, Program Version, Computation Interval), compares
    with the files on disk and flags unregistered plans, entries without files, stray copies (renamed .hdf, .tmp.hdf,
    snapshot HDFs, Backup.p##, sync conflict copies), plans sharing a flow file under different storm titles and
    generic plan titles. Never treat stray copies as results. Fill the condition, terrain and status (live /
    superseded) columns and keep the register in the model folder.
12. Confirm each plan's flow file matches its title/storm; separate titles or clearly named plans for existing vs
    proposed; rename generic plan titles to condition-specific names (on a copy) before results are reported.
13. FLO-2D archives: register every native folder (build, grid, run time, terrain changes vs base, levee/barrier
    records); diff each alternative grid against the base; match folders to report figures; never select by folder
    name or newest timestamp; separate artificial levee barriers from real proposed grading.
14. Terrain packages: list Terrain folder sizes and each scenario .vrt source and cell size; scenario modifications
    live in the terrain HDF or geometry, not the tif; identify duplicate source tiles; check stored maps' Terrain
    name and StoredFilename and regenerate missing maps.
15. Open in the same or newer RAS version on a copy only (opening rewrites plan and geometry files); record versions;
    a 7.x set is not upgraded or mixed into 6.6 work without a logged decision (D02).
16. Run and store models on a local non-synced drive; copy only final plan results to the synced share; delete
    .tmp.hdf and unused plan results before archiving (on the working copy).
17. Every caption and table that uses results cites plan file, short ID and geometry (report-writer applies this).

### E. Public data, terrain, records, reference documents
18. Public GIS and hydrology data: `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\rest_harvest.py" --config <harvest.json> --out <job>\02_Data\GIS_Public\<YYYYMMDD>`
    (envelope query with paging, GeoJSON per layer, GeoPackage per theme in the GIS venv, `_download_log.csv`; one
    dead service is logged and the pass continues). Layer list and rainfall/soils/land-cover rules:
    `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` A. Resolve every ERR row before hydrology starts.
19. Terrain: `reference/terrain_dem_build.md` - extent over all contributing watersheds, TNM item list, tiles chosen
    by acquisition collection and logged (D53), clip before mosaic, project CRS, m->ft, DEMs at 3 ft (3.28 ft for
    native 1 m) for hydraulics/grading, 10 ft for hydrology, 30 ft for large basins (D54), per-source cell counts for
    composites, vintage differencing.
20. Record plans and field books: `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` B (catalog queries, page budget, SHA-256 and
    magic bytes, OCR with orientation, strict utf-8, deterministic quotes, numbers checked on the page image, crossing
    details accepted only when spatially anchored).
21. Reference documents: `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` C (copy unaltered, hash, page-aware extraction, OCR only
    low-text PDFs, encrypted PDFs left pending, human decisions in a separate sheet).

### F. CRS, units, vertical datum and the data log (DSO-C05; D55)
22. Start `02_Data\<Job>_DataLog_<YYYYMMDD>.md` from `reference/data_log_template.md`. Project CRS by jurisdiction from
    the survey basis; Pima County default NAD83(HARN) Arizona Central, intl ft, EPSG:2868 (D55, default, to confirm).
    Record the realization of every layer; mixing realizations is flagged.
23. Do not trust declared EPSG/.prj metadata: compare at least 3 known points to the model grid for every incoming
    CAD/GIS/LandXML file and log the result.
24. Local site coordinates: apply the documented local-to-State Plane transform (translate, rotate, scale about the
    base point); preserve CAD arcs with a chord tolerance before transforming.
25. Find the vertical datum and benchmark note in the survey; if absent, request it and mark dependent elevations
    (pads, floors vs modeled WSE) provisional.
26. Reconcile units (metric survey vs ft plans) before any grid update.
27. LandXML: P order is northing, easting, elevation; interpolate on the original triangles, exclude invisible faces,
    no extrapolation across voids; update the grid from the original survey triangles, not a new triangulation.
28. Compare the new survey surface with the model grid/DEM (mean, std dev); list differences over 2 ft and explain them.
29. Received model sets: read RASProjectionFilename in the .rasmap, the SRS of each .vrt and each delivered .prj;
    confirm the same horizontal realization and units (e.g. EPSG:2230 vs 6426 in California) and vertical datum;
    record the CRS of each layer before any reprojection.

### G. Findings and scope (DSO-C13)
30. Write numbered findings (F01, F02 ...) with severity, evidence locator (report page, model file) and action, in
    `00_Admin\<Job>_Intake_Findings_<YYYYMMDD>.md`. Issue only after the inventory is final.
31. Write the scope as plain text: one page target, two pages max, no subtasks, with assumptions and exclusions; list
    conditional services (FEMA map revision, regional model rebuild, easement-driven redesign) separately.
32. Hand off to `due-diligence-researcher` (prior and adjacent studies, existing conditions, jurisdiction
    confirmation) with the inventory, data log, model registers and findings.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
- `addons/pima-county-rfcd.md`: lidar collections and composite rule, target CRS (D55).
- `addons/fema.md`: NFHL layer set, LOMR check, screening vs duplicate-effective wording.
- `addons/caltrans-california.md`: tenth-postmile points, AADT, dam inundation; California CRS realization check.
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md`: Maps and Records catalog and field books.
- Arizona jurisdictions with a county manual use the manual's rainfall and soils sources (`drainage-report-build`
  add-on of that agency).

## Gotchas
- The folder showed only desktop.ini until a manual download; the run stalled about 1 h (TANGERINE-009).
- A bulk upload created a full nested duplicate of the project folder inside itself (about 2,258 files, 50 GB),
  about 3 h to sync (TANGERINE-009).
- OneDrive resets file timestamps to the sync time, so file dates cannot be used to estimate work history; keep a
  dated log (TANGERINE-009).
- The upload grew from 1,726 to 2,653 files during the review; findings from the first snapshot had to be revised
  (NORTHLOOP-001).
- Correspondence did not show prior agency approval of the old report (NORTHLOOP-001).
- The prior report carried conflicting dates and tables (Q500 basis stated two ways); do not reuse tables without
  tracing to calcs (NORTHLOOP-001).
- Plan p01 (floodwall, existing event) existed on disk with a 1.5 GB result HDF and was cited in the delivered data
  dictionary, but was not registered in the .prj, so it did not appear in the RAS plan list; add the plan back through
  the .prj or open the .p01 directly (DLR-001).
- A stray renamed copy of a plan result HDF (p02 with extra letters appended) was the same size as the real one; easy
  to map the wrong file (DLR-001).
- RAS Mapper listed a 91% snapshot HDF as a results layer next to the completed run; check the layer name for Snapshot
  before mapping (DLR-001).
- One geometry HDF appeared twice in RAS Mapper under two names, and a stub geometry HDF (0 MB) was referenced but not
  in the .prj (DLR-001).
- Plans mixed 30 s and 1 s computation intervals and RAS 6.70 / 7.00 / 7.01 files; a test plan created after receipt
  changed the project Current Plan; record the as-received Current Plan before editing (DLR-001).
- The .rasmap projection was set from a feature shapefile .prj under Features rather than the Terrain Projection.prj;
  it matched, but this is fragile when features are replaced (DLR-002).
- Delivered spot elevation points were in NAD83(2011) CA zone 6 ftUS (EPSG:6426) while all sampled rasters were NAD83
  CA zone 6 ftUS (EPSG:2230); a silent realization mismatch of up to a few ft if a GIS transforms on the fly (DLR-002).
- The base terrain was one 53 GB tif at 0.615 ft cells (about 430,000 px square) plus a 2.2 GB terrain HDF; the three
  scenario terrains were VRTs over that same tif (DLR-003).
- Stored depth maps referenced terrain clone names that were not delivered and output folders that did not exist, so
  they would not display until recomputed (DLR-003).
- The same USGS and county DEM tiles were delivered twice in two Terrain subfolders, including two 6.8 GB county DEM
  copies (DLR-003).
- Report and figure captions cited existing conditions as Plan 12 / EX_<init>_LG, but p12 was titled Plan 12 with no
  short ID (geometry g08), the project notes named p09 EX_<init> as existing, and no plan carried EX_<init>_LG
  (TANGERINE-004).
- 12 plans and 8 geometries in one project with superseded iterations p01-p08 make the wrong HDF easy to read; confirm
  the plan before exporting rasters (TANGERINE-004).
- Plans p05 (100-yr) and p06 (10-yr) both pointed to flow file u02 - the 10-yr run either used 100-yr flows or the file
  was overwritten between runs; it matched a mislabeled-storm comment on the draft (SAHPARK-016).
- OneDrive sync created a conflict copy of the g04 geometry .hdf (225 MB) (SAHPARK-016).
- The same 8 USGS tiles were copied into three terrain folders (SAHPARK-016).
- About 40 geometry saves (g02) and 19 saves (g04) in Backup show heavy iteration on berm and road terrain
  (SAHPARK-016).
- A folder named Alt1 had an eastern channel and 2,120 ft of artificial barriers, while the report's preferred
  alternative left the east natural (NORTHLOOP-006).
- Both named 500-yr folders were empty; the old 500-yr used a 1.75 x Q100 multiplier, not a saved run (NORTHLOOP-006).
- The NHD MapServer timed out at 180 s, then returned empty JSON on retry (4 passes); fall back to the staged HU8
  shapefile zip from the TNM S3 bucket (CALFIRE-003).
- Shapefiles truncate field names over 10 characters; keep the GeoPackage as master (CALFIRE-003).
- Log failures instead of stopping the loop so one dead service does not cost the whole pass (CALFIRE-003).
- PFDS returns JavaScript text (result = values; quantiles = [...]), not JSON; parse the arrays (CALFIRE-005).
- Dual groups (B/D, C/D) and Not rated units (3-6%) need a stated rule before CN assignment (CALFIRE-005).
- Display-clipped polygons must not feed hydraulic encroachment logic (SILVERBELL-013).
- An updated local model plus mapped lines is a screening, not a duplicate-effective model (SILVERBELL-013).
- Tiles carry 2-3 overlapping vintages (2017, 2019, 2025) and duplicate NED entries; filter or the mosaic mixes
  surfaces (CALFIRE-004).
- Newest-published logic picked the older 2018 collection (published 2025) on several tiles; fixed with a
  collection-preference step and a DEM rebuild (RKN-002).
- The initial DEM extent did not cover the full offsite watersheds; extending it changed several CP inputs and forced
  PC-Hydro reruns (RKN-002).
- A 107-tile merged input built a 20 GB terrain tif; clip first (DLR-007).
- Street and wash network shapefiles ended up listed under Terrains in the .rasmap (DLR-007).
- The USGS 2021 10-ft DEM contributed 0 cells to the composite and the run continued without noticing (SAH-020).
- Large changes (30 to 80 ft mean over hundreds of ac) were mine tailings growth, which affects depression volumes and
  flow paths (SAH-020).
- 1.8 GB of raw tiles per site (CALFIRE-004).
- Culvert inverts read from lidar are estimates only; carry as open items until survey (CALFIRE-004).
- USGS 1 m tiles are NAD83 UTM 12N in meters; convert to ft and compare to survey before use (DLR-007, STARVALLEY-014).
- The DLR-007 terrain lessons come from a test project, not the received set (DLR-007).
- LandXML declared EPSG:2223 but was in local coordinates; watershed and parcel shapefiles likewise had State Plane .prj
  files with local coordinates (STARVALLEY-014).
- Old channel files sat about 50 ft off the true centerline (STARVALLEY-014).
- One CAD vertex differed by 100 ft and was excluded (STARVALLEY-014).
- Survey CAD had no datum or benchmark statement; pad elevation and WSE remain provisional (NORTHLOOP-019).
- An early Delaunay terrain was replaced by exact LandXML triangles (26,507 cells updated) (NORTHLOOP-019).
- DCR vertical datum unknown; EG vs FG differences are not earthwork depths (SILVERBELL-007).
- The first field-book search stopped at page 1 and called the target missing (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Sideways scans gave zero OCR hits on all 26 pages until orientation was corrected (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Default cp1252 decoding failed on utf-8 OCR text (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Free-form model quotes: only 40 of 137 matched the source exactly (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- OCR misread 2698.20 as 2696.20 on one record; two monuments with the same elevation were different points
  (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Plan titles naming roads do not geolocate a structure; candidate crossing details stayed unaccepted until spatially
  anchored (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- 8 datum/crossing retrieval tasks, 5 failed or empty (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- A 715-file reference intake ran 5.3 h; 220 of 264 PDFs verified, 16 timeouts, 18 page-label failures, 8 zero-text
  (EKOS-LOCAL-023).
- A stdout warning on a successful extraction made the orchestrator mark failure; judge by exit code and output
  artifact (EKOS-LOCAL-023).
- OCR of map pages misread labels (EKOS-LOCAL-023).
- Qdrant 1.15.3 accepted but did not return collection metadata; verify the fingerprint in point payloads instead
  (EKOS-LOCAL-022).
- LM Studio rejected the json_object response format (HTTP 400) (EKOS-LOCAL-022, EKOS-LOCAL-005).
- Only a synthetic 5-page test passed retrieval qualification; real manuals are not yet qualified (EKOS-LOCAL-022).

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('crs')`, `get_qc_rules('existing-conditions')`, `get_qc_rules('model-runs')`, plus the
  jurisdiction tag.
- Inventory final (no growth since last snapshot) before findings are issued; copy verification log (count, bytes,
  hash sample) present (NORTHLOOP-001, TANGERINE-009).
- Every cited plan exists, is registered, carries a condition-specific title and matches the caption; plan flow file
  matches plan title/storm (HYD-C13).
- `_download_log.csv` has no unresolved ERR rows before hydrology starts; HSG rule for dual/not-rated units stated in
  the assumption log (DSO-C03).
- Per-source cell count in a composite (any source with 0 cells stops the run); nodata fraction 0 inside the
  contributing area; DEM extent covers every contributing watershed (DSO-C04).
- Known-point check (at least 3 points) logged for every incoming CAD/GIS/LandXML file; vertical datum and benchmark
  stated for every survey used to set an elevation, otherwise labelled provisional; survey vs grid difference table
  with differences over 2 ft explained (DSO-C05).
- Every number taken from a record checked against the page image; every quoted excerpt matches the source
  byte-for-byte (DSO-C06).
- Data log names the realization of every layer (D55) and the cell size of every DEM (D54).

- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters DSO-C13, DSO-C04, DSO-C03, DSO-C06, DSO-C05, DSO-C09 and the intake part of
  HYD-C13 (steps 1-10; step 11 citation rule handed to report-writer); decisions D53, D54, D55 (default, to confirm:
  Pima County EPSG:2868), D56, plus D02, D11, D14. Added scripts intake_inventory.py, ras_plan_register.py,
  rest_harvest.py (tested on sample folders, a synthetic RAS project and a local mock REST service; live public
  services were not reachable from the build container) and reference files for data log, terrain build, public GIS,
  records and reference documents.

## Skill: pchydro-hydrographs v2.0.0

# PC-Hydro: inputs, runs, hydrograph QC and DSS

End-to-end PC-Hydro workflow: **get basin inputs (report extract or GIS build) -> run them on the
PC-Hydro website (interactive or batch) -> save native printouts, hydrographs and .pk6 -> QC the
export and make the audited routing copy -> build RAS + HMS DSS files.**

The website is always how peaks and hydrographs are produced; there is no offline PC-Hydro engine.
Keep the `.pk6` inputs so any run can be repeated by hand if the web app changes.

## When to use
- Peaks, program printouts or 1-min hydrographs are needed for watersheds under 1 sq mi in Pima
  County RFCD jurisdiction (or a jurisdiction that accepts PC-Hydro; see add-ons).
- A prior report's basin inputs must be re-entered to rebuild its hydrographs.
- Many small watersheds on a large site, or offsite washes entering a model domain, need CPs, `.pk6`
  files and inflow hydrographs (Phase 1b).
- PC-Hydro hydrographs must go into HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, FLO-2D or a report table.
Not for watersheds over 1 sq mi in Pima County: route those to hechms-headless.

## Inputs
- Source of basin parameters: report PDF/Excel/Word (confirm the table or appendix with the user), or
  a conditioned DEM plus land-use, soil and structure inventory for a GIS build.
- Scenario list: CPs, conditions (existing/proposed), return periods.
- Run log for the project (`00_Admin/run_log`) with the D17 terms-approval line.
- For QC: reported peaks (from the export itself) and, for rebuilds, the old report's peaks.
- Saved NOAA Atlas 14 upper 90% depth arrays per CP (comparison array, D21).

## Operating rules
- **Confirm the source document and the table/appendix** holding the basin parameters before
  extracting. Parsing is heuristic: show the parsed values and have the user confirm before running.
- **Terms of use (D17):** JCO approval is recorded once per project in the run log; after that,
  interactive and batch runs click I Agree without asking again. If the line is missing, ask JCO
  once and write it (default, to confirm).
- **Run mode (D18):** interactive (browser automation tool on a visible browser) for a few CPs;
  batch (Playwright, Edge channel, headless or isolated window) for more than a few. Both are
  supported; the batch is the standard for 10+ CPs.
- **Native inputs:** use the native runoff parameters for the selected cover and soil group; no fixed
  CN (e.g. CN 86) carried in. Vegetation on graded ground = program default, 20% per NORTHLOOP-013,
  verified against the 7.4 auto-fill before each batch; the old 5% Desert Brush rule is removed
  (D20, default, to confirm). Valid watershed types include Mixed / Undeveloped-Valley.
- **Tc** = the program value, 5 min minimum. Never call time to peak "Tc".
- **Rainfall (D21):** the in-app Fetch Rainfall governs; script-written depths are only the
  comparison array; record the Atlas 14 edition served.
- **Preparer:** userName = `Psomas (<initials>)` before Calculate.
- **Peaks and series (D19):** the native export is kept unchanged as the record; a separate
  peak-adjusted copy is used for routing with the added volume logged; the QC workbook reports both
  the sampled max and the program-reported peak. Report tables use the program-reported peak.
  New reports: native output is the reference (0.0 cfs tolerance). Rebuilds: the old report is the
  target.
- **DSS output is v7 only** (the only version writable from the container). INST-VAL, CFS, 1Minute.
- One PC-Hydro version per analysis, stated the same in criteria, methods, results and the software
  register.
- Deliver downloadable files for everything (CSV, XLSX, PDF, .pk6, DSS) and list them.

## Steps

### Phase 1: Extract basin inputs from a report
1. `python3 scripts/extract_basin_inputs.py --in <report.pdf|.xlsx|.docx> --out-stem <stem>`
   (EKOS: GIS venv python by full path). Produces `<stem>_basin_inputs.csv` (area, CN, C, Tc, lag,
   % impervious, reported Q by return period) and `<stem>_report_text.txt` for manual review.
2. Refine by hand where the report layout defeats the regex. Show the table; get the user's
   confirmation before any run.

### Phase 1b: GIS build of CPs and .pk6 files (large sites, offsite inflows)
1. Gather the structure inventory: master plan inventory and DOT as-builts (size, station, invert)
   for each cross-culvert or entry point.
2. Condition the DEM (10 ft or finer per D54 hydrology grid; WhiteboxTools least-cost breach, D8
   pointer and accumulation, streams >= 5 ac, slope). Close rasterio datasets explicitly.
3. Place CPs by rule: IN (offsite inflow >= 5 ac), OUTR/OUTX (exits across an exclusion or other
   boundary), junctions, and one CP per cross-culvert.
4. Build incremental and total watersheds, longest watercourses, segment slopes, land-use and soil
   overlays. Run the nested-area check (drainage-report-build) before any flows are summed.
5. Write one PC-Hydro 7.4 `.pk6` (JSON) per CP under 1 sq mi. Atlas 14 upper 90% depths at the
   centroid may be written as the comparison array (D21). Do not hard-code vegetation density.
   CPs over 1 sq mi go to hechms-headless.
6. Where the watershed to a culvert cannot be defined, use culvert capacity as the upper bound of
   inflow and say so in the inflow register.
7. Keep a tracked rerun list for CPs whose inputs change after a DEM extension.

### Phase 2: Run PC-Hydro (choose mode)
- **Interactive (few CPs):** follow `reference/pchydro_web_workflow.md`.
- **Batch (more than a few CPs):** follow `reference/pchydro_batch_automation.md` (probe, vegetation
  auto-fill check, per-CP loop, failed-CP rerun).
Both modes, per CP:
1. Load the `.pk6` via File > Open (initialize the dialog before setting the file input); wait for
   the CP field to populate. Name the CP field with the basin id.
2. Set userName; read back every native input and compare to the source; quantize flow-length
   segments to whole ft summing to the native total and soil shares to whole percent by largest
   remainder; log each precision change; stop the CP on any other mismatch.
3. Coordinates at 4 decimals; in-app Fetch Rainfall; wait for Matches and the 100-yr 1-hr value;
   compare at 2 decimals; record the edition.
4. Calculate; wait until calcDate changes and qp100 is filled; read q100 and tc100.
5. Save the program PDF (check content-type is application/pdf), the 1-min hydrograph CSV and the
   recomputed `.pk6`; write hashes and a peaks table.
6. Log failed CPs and rerun only those.

### Phase 3: Offsite and model inflows (when hydrographs feed a model)
1. Enter each flow as an inflow BC at the culvert outlet or domain edge.
2. Add every inflow to the model inflow register with its source (study, new PC-Hydro run, or
   capacity bound).
3. Run with the PC-Hydro version the reviewing agency accepts.

### Phase 4: Export QC and audited routing copy (D19, HJR-C03)
1. Run:
   `python3 scripts/hydrographs_to_xlsx.py --out <CPs>_hydrographs.xlsx --adjusted-csv <CPs>_routing.csv --native-csv <CPs>_native.csv [--targets old_report_peaks.csv] <CP-*.csv>`
   - Reads native exports (reported peak from the `Peak Discharge:` line) or plain tables plus
     `--peaks` (series, reported_peak_cfs [, equation_volume_acft]).
   - Sheets: `Peaks` (sampled max and time, reported peak, difference, report table value, native and
     adjusted integrated volume, peak-adjust and tail-close added volume, equation volume, target
     comparison), `Adjustment_Log`, `Native` (unchanged), `Peak_Adjusted` (series `_ADJ`).
   - Exit code 2 when any flag is raised (step not 60 s, no reported peak, reported below sampled,
     target mismatch). Resolve or explain each flag before Phase 5.
2. Confirm the actual sample spacing is 60 s (the script checks the file, not the UI setting).
3. Expect the sampled max to differ from the reported peak; the adjusted copy replaces the maximum
   ordinate with the reported peak. A reported peak below the sampled max is not adjusted; it is
   flagged for review against the printout.
4. Report equation runoff volume, integrated hydrograph volume and adjustment volume separately. Do
   not reject an export because they differ; there is no volume-equality gate.
5. Nonzero tails are closed with one extra minute to 0 cfs in the adjusted copy; the added volume is
   logged.
6. Peak QC: new reports compare the report table to the reported peak at 0.0 cfs; rebuilds compare to
   the old report's peaks (`--targets`, `--target-tol` if JCO sets one). Resolve discrepancies before
   building DSS.
7. Offer an overlay plot of native vs adjusted hydrographs for QC (kept in 40_QC, D30).

### Phase 5: Build DSS for RAS and HMS
1. Use the routing CSV from Phase 4 (first column `Time_min`, one cfs column per series, `_ADJ`
   names). If the script wrote `_gridN` files, the series are on different time grids: re-export at
   1 min rather than mixing grids.
2. `python3 scripts/build_dss.py --csv <CPs>_routing.csv --out-stem <stem> --variant both --apart <PROJCODE>`
   writes `<stem>_RAS.dss` (A-part blank) and `<stem>_HMS.dss` (A-part = project code).
3. Reopen each DSS and verify every ordinate, interval, units, type and volume against the routing CSV
   (`reference/dss_formats.md`, round-trip check).
4. Check whether the RAS model reads DSS or inline hydrographs before choosing the BC method
   (`reference/dss_formats.md`).

### Phase 6: Deliver
1. Deliver: native exports, program PDFs, `.pk6` files, QC workbook, routing CSV, both DSS files,
   hashes, run log.
2. Note that HEC-HMS gages and HEC-RAS DSS BCs must be **repointed and the pathname re-selected**,
   and that models must be **recomputed** (model-run-supervisor rerun gate).
3. Report appendix: native printouts and native hydrograph exports (D38). The adjusted copy and its
   added-volume log go in the hydrology QC note, not in place of the native output.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
No addons/ files in this skill; jurisdiction rules for method selection live in drainage-report-build
add-ons. Load the relevant one before Phase 1:
- `get_skill("drainage-report-build", resource="addons/pima-county-rfcd.md")`: PC-Hydro 7.4 is the
  accepted method under 1 sq mi (TECH-015, TECH-018); HEC-HMS TR-55 parameters over 1 sq mi; NOAA
  Atlas 14 upper 90%; Tc program value, 5 min minimum. Confirm the version the agency accepts when
  reusing an older study (ELTORO-009).
- `addons/town-of-marana.md`: PC-Hydro for non-regional (onsite) flows only, MDM 4.1 (D24, default,
  to confirm); Marana thresholds 10 sq mi / 180 min; graded-ground default cover rule observed on
  Marana onsite work (NORTHLOOP-013).
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md`, `addons/town-of-sahuarita.md`: confirm which method and study govern
  before running; Sahuarita published basin-study flows may replace new runs.
- Pima County RFCD + ADOT offsite inflows: culvert data from ADOT as-builts; PC-Hydro for each
  watershed under 1 sq mi (RKN-003).

## Gotchas
- App JS is obfuscated; button/field names and page functions (openProject, fillSCS, hydroCalc,
  hydroGraph, printFile) had to be found with probe scripts before automation worked
  (RKN-004, SAH-007).
- Vegetation density auto-fill behaviour had to be probed from the live page; confirm default cover
  densities match the PC-Hydro guide before a batch (SAH-007).
- File-chooser events timed out until the File-Open dialog was initialized properly
  (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- Soils 52.263/41.418/6.318% rounded to 52/41/6 (total 99) failed validation; largest remainder
  52/42/6 passed (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- Full-precision GIS lengths failed the native length-sum check (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- Never set fake valid flags or force Calculate enabled (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- Direct HTTP rainfall request returned 403; use the in-app fetch (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- The PC-Hydro guide cites an older Atlas 14 edition than the data now served; record the edition
  fetched (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- pdf.php sometimes returns text/html instead of a PDF (seen at CP-103); check content-type and retry
  the CP (RKN-004).
- A local CORS helper server (127.0.0.1 with private-network headers) was used first to feed records
  to a tab; the Playwright file-input route is simpler (RKN-004, SAH-007).
- 67 subbasins ran in about 25 min once the batch worked (SAH-007).
- Web app changes can break the batch; keep the .pk6 inputs so runs can be repeated by hand (SAH-007).
- 9 failed PC-Hydro tasks on one project before the adapter was stable (NOAA mapping x3, basin
  import x4, road scenario x1, benchmark) (EKOS-LOCAL-006).
- Window move/resize re-renders the page and resets state (pchydro-hydrographs v1).
- Match the in-file Concentration Point field to the basin id; scripts key off it, not the filename
  (pchydro-hydrographs v1).
- Owner correction: at steps other than 1 min the peak never matches and has to be adjusted by hand;
  export at 1 min and use the audited adjustment (EKOS-LOCAL-007).
- An invented 1% volume-equality gate wrongly flagged an export as corrupt; the county manual defines
  the hydrograph integral as an approximation (EKOS-LOCAL-007).
- The export QC applied across 4 catchment scenario sets on one project (benchmark, basin, road
  crossing, HMS inflows) (EKOS-LOCAL-007).
- data_type not INST-VAL makes HMS read all zeros (pchydro-hydrographs v1 dss_formats).
- Saved standards still carried the old 5% Desert Brush graded-ground rule; JCO's correction
  overrides it; purge it wherever found (NORTHLOOP-013).
- rasterio prints "NoneType has no attribute exc_info" tracebacks at interpreter exit; harmless;
  close datasets explicitly to keep logs clean (RKN-003).
- CPs whose inputs changed after a DEM extension need a tracked rerun list so carried results stay
  consistent (RKN-003).
- The source report covered only the central reach; north and south reaches had no culvert
  inventory and had to be scoped as new work (ELTORO-009).
- A reviewer had already questioned the PC-Hydro version used in the source report; confirm the
  version with the agency first (ELTORO-009).

## QC checks
Pull: `get_qc_rules('hydrology')`, plus `get_qc_rules('pima-rfcd')` / `('marana')` / `('tucson')` /
`('sahuarita')` by jurisdiction, and `get_qc_rules('model-runs')` when hydrographs feed a model.
This skill must pass before hand-off:
- Terms-approval line present in the run log (D17).
- Native input read-back matches scenario values field by field before Calculate; every precision
  change logged.
- No manually typed vegetation density or fixed CN on graded ground unless JCO approved it (D20).
- Fetched rainfall matches the saved Atlas 14 upper 90% arrays at 2 decimals; edition recorded (D21).
- Printout PDF content-type is application/pdf; userName shows `Psomas (<initials>)`.
- Export step is 60 s in the file; units cfs.
- Peaks sheet shows sampled max and reported peak for every series; report tables use the reported
  peak; new reports match native at 0.0 cfs; rebuilds compared to the old report (D19).
- Adjusted copy is separate from the native export; added volumes logged; no volume-equality gate.
- DSS round trip verified ordinate by ordinate; INST-VAL, CFS, 1Minute.
- Every inflow BC appears in the inflow register with its source.
- One PC-Hydro version stated throughout the report and software register.
